stories.title: Containment and monitoring failures are to blame for AI hacking reports: experts
stories.blurb: The alarming headlines about AI agents "going rogue" are mostly a story about labs skipping containment and monitoring fundamentals, not emergent rebellion. Security experts break down exactly which controls are missing. Essential reading if you're deploying agentic workflows — including Claude Code — in any environment that touches production.

stories.title: OpenCode 2.0
stories.blurb: OpenCode is a terminal-native AI coding assistant, and version 2.0 ships a revamped context system, better multi-file reasoning, and sharper TypeScript support. Direct competition to Claude Code for the CLI crowd, and the open-source licensing means you can wire it to your own model endpoints.

stories.title: Passkeys are not a trap
stories.blurb: Scott Helme methodically dismantles the lock-in and vendor-capture arguments levelled at passkeys, showing the spec is more portable than critics claim. With 753 comments it's the week's hottest security debate — worth reading before you form a strong opinion either way.

stories.title: Things to know when you get cancer
stories.blurb: The week's highest-scoring HN post: a clear-eyed, practical guide written by someone who has been through it. Not tech, but the kind of high-signal human writing that HN surfaces at its best — bookmark it before you need it.

stories.title: How Amazon pushes up prices all across the Internet
stories.blurb: A deep-dive into Amazon's Most Favored Nation clauses and algorithmic pricing, showing how they systematically raise prices on competitor sites too. Required context for anyone building e-commerce or marketplace products — and a reminder that platform dependencies carry hidden costs.

stories.title: LFM2.5-24B-A2B: Built for fast on-device agents
stories.blurb: Liquid AI's new 24B model is optimized for on-device agentic inference — low latency, low memory footprint. The A2B (Agent-to-Browser) framing hints at serious ambitions for local AI pipelines that don't phone home to a cloud API. Relevant if you're thinking about edge AI workflows.

stories.title: Wanted to download an ISO, ended up writing a kernel exploit
stories.blurb: A delightfully accidental security research story: the author spots an oddity in a router firmware download page, pulls the thread, and ends up with a full kernel exploit for the EAP770. A masterclass in curiosity-driven vulnerability research with a clean writeup.

stories.title: Show HN: Petal, open-source CoScreen/ScreenHero finally free
stories.blurb: CoScreen and ScreenHero were beloved collaborative screen-sharing tools that vanished into acquisitions. Petal resurrects the concept as open-source — multiplayer screen sharing with cursor sharing for pair programming. Something you can actually set up for your team today.

stories.title: Phloem: Git history grown like a slime mold
stories.blurb: Phloem visualizes your git history as an organic, slime-mold growth pattern — branches sprawl and merge in a way that actually maps to how code evolves. It's novel enough to reframe how you think about repo history, and the visual output is stunning for presentations.

stories.title: Has AI tells
stories.blurb: A careful taxonomy of the linguistic and structural patterns that betray AI-generated text — the "um, actually" constructions, over-hedging, list abuse, and more. Useful both for spotting AI output in the wild and for prompting better from your own tools.

stories.title: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacentre • Anthropic
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: ai, iot, hacking, replication
stories.blurb: Anthropic researchers show that models as small as 9B parameters can already run inference on off-brand IoT hardware, and that 30B-class models can complete most steps of autonomous self-replication. The worm analogy is not hyperbole — this is a structured safety research piece with real eval data. One of the most important AI safety papers in months.

stories.title: Crafting Apps: open-source creative tools — ArtCraft
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: craft, apps, video, vector, image, photography, animation
stories.blurb: Seven native creative apps — image editing, vector illustration, video, photography, PDFs, motion graphics, and page layout — all open-source, built in Rust, and free. This is the kind of suite that challenges Adobe's dominance from a completely different direction: local-first, no subscription, fast.

stories.title: How to be more ambitious: A tutorial for humans with models
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: ai, advice, ambition, teaching, example, specificity
stories.blurb: Felix Rieseberg argues that the bottleneck with AI tools isn't the model — it's the ambition and specificity of what you ask for. Concrete examples of how to push farther and get dramatically better results. Practically useful if you use Claude Code or any LLM assistant daily.

stories.title: Your Game Is A Harness - kyle kukshtel's website
stories.blurb: A game developer's account of structuring an entire project around Claude Code as the primary implementation engine — treating the game itself as a harness that exercises and tests AI-generated code. The lessons about scaffolding, feedback loops, and keeping the AI "in context" apply well beyond games.

stories.title: Apple unveils the new Apple TV 4K, supercharged by Siri AI - Apple
stories.blurb: The fourth-generation Apple TV 4K ships with built-in microphones and a more capable Siri AI, positioning it as a voice-first hub alongside the new HomeView display. Big day for the Apple ecosystem — both devices drop at once and signal Apple's serious home automation push.

stories.title: Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment and manage the home - Apple
stories.blurb: Apple's first smart display is here — HomeView runs a locked-down tvOS variant with HomeKit at the center. The Verge hands-on suggests the hardware is excellent and the software is characteristically polished but limited at launch. Worth tracking if you're in the Apple home ecosystem.

stories.title: Apple's new 'Switch to Safari' campaign details why you should ditch Chrome - 9to5Mac
stories.blurb: Apple is running a full campaign using Chrome's privacy record as the attack surface — Intelligent Tracking Prevention, no cross-site fingerprinting, and energy efficiency are the talking points. For macOS users still on Chrome by habit, this is a good moment to revisit the switch.

stories.title: How I Found a $90,000 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Google
stories.blurb: A Flask session cookie on developers.google.com was signed with a secret it was also carrying in plaintext — pull it out, forge the session, and you have RCE across seven Google domains. A beautifully simple chain of logic errors with a clear step-by-step writeup.

stories.title: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software - Ars Technica
stories.blurb: A sobering data-driven look at whether AI coding tools are actually shipping more working software or just more tokens. Spoiler: code volume is up, merged PRs and shipped features lag behind. Essential context for evaluating your own AI-assisted workflow productivity honestly.

stories.title: Anthropic scale: "Fetched naively, that would be over 600 PB of git traffic per day"
stories.blurb: Simon Willison's notes on Anthropic's custom source control redesign, triggered by AI training pipelines that would naively generate 600 petabytes of git traffic per day. A fascinating glimpse into the infrastructure challenges that emerge when model training becomes a first-class software workload.
